evals.prompt: Commit and push my changes in /tmp/eval-ship-1-ws. It's a pnpm TypeScript project and I'm already on feat/parser-add-csv-reader. I added a CSV reader and a test for it.
evals.expected_output: Agent sees it is already on a feature branch and does not create a new one. Detects pnpm from pnpm-lock.yaml, runs 'pnpm run format' and 'pnpm run lint:fix', verifies with the repo's own scripts, shows git status and the staged file list, commits with a conventional subject such as 'feat(parser): add CSV reader' and a body, adds no Co-Authored-By trailer of its own and leaves attribution to the harness. The request named the push in the same sentence as the commit, so the agent pushes without asking again. Finds no PR on the branch and does not open one.
expectations: Agent checks the current branch and confirms it is not the repo's default branch before committing
Agent does NOT create a new branch because the repo is already on a feature branch
Agent reads git worktree list, finds the branch's existing worktree or works in the current one, and does NOT create a second worktree for the same branch
Agent detects pnpm as the package manager, referencing pnpm-lock.yaml or the packageManager field
Agent runs the repo's own format and lint fix scripts via pnpm rather than ad-hoc commands
Agent shows git status and the staged file list before committing
Agent uses a conventional commit subject under 72 characters
Agent adds no Co-Authored-By trailer of its own and leaves attribution to the harness; no agent session link or model name appears
Agent pushes without asking a second time, because the request named the push in one sentence with the commit
Agent checks whether the branch already has a PR and, finding none, does NOT open one, since the user did not ask for a PR

evals.prompt: I finished the retry logic in /tmp/eval-ship-2-ws. Please commit it.
evals.expected_output: The repo is sitting on main. Agent refuses to commit on main, creates a branch named per Conventional Commits such as feat/client-add-retry-logic, creates it in its own worktree under .claude/worktrees/ after checking git worktree list for an existing one, then formats, lint-fixes, verifies, stages with .claude/ and docs/plans/ excluded, and commits. Does not push and does not open a PR because neither was asked for; if it offers to go further, it asks and waits.
expectations: Agent detects that the current branch is main and refuses to commit on it
Agent creates a new branch before committing, named <type>/<scope>-<description>
Agent checks git worktree list before creating, then creates the branch in a worktree under .claude/worktrees/ and works from there
Agent runs the repo's package.json scripts for format and lint fix
Agent excludes .claude/, docs/plans/ and .plans/ from the staged files
Agent commits with a conventional commit message on the new branch
Agent does NOT push, since the request was 'commit' and a push needs its own yes
Agent does NOT open a pull request

evals.prompt: Commit and push my work in /tmp/eval-ship-3-ws. Heads up, the pre-commit hook has been strict lately.
evals.expected_output: Agent branches if needed, formats, lint-fixes, stages and commits. The pre-commit hook fails on a type error in src/client.ts. Agent reads the hook output, fixes the actual type error rather than suppressing it, runs verify again on the fixed tree, re-stages, and retries. The second attempt succeeds. The request named the push, so the agent pushes after the fix without a further ask, and reports what was root-caused.
expectations: Agent attempts a commit that fails on the pre-commit hook
Agent does NOT use --no-verify and does not disable or delete the hook
Agent reads the hook output and fixes the root cause in the file the hook named
Agent does NOT suppress the error with a cast, an ignore comment, or a weakened test
Agent runs verify again on the fixed tree before re-staging, rather than reusing the run from before the fix
Agent re-stages the fixed files and retries the commit
Agent stays within 3 commit attempts
Agent pushes without a further ask, since the request named the push, and does NOT open a PR
Agent reports which hook failure was fixed and how

evals.prompt: Commit, push and open a PR for /tmp/eval-ship-4-ws. The change adds token refresh to the auth package.
evals.expected_output: Agent branches if on main, runs format, lint:fix and verification, stages cleanly, commits with a conventional message, then pushes and opens the PR without asking again, because the one sentence named both. After the commit it checks that the committed tree equals the staged tree and that nothing verify saw was left unstaged, and only then labels the verify run with the commit's sha. It runs pr-desc in create mode, handing over that block and the head sha, and opens a draft PR whose title is a Conventional Commit subject and whose body has Summary, Trade-offs, Follow-ups and a Verification section with one bullet per command that ran, each with its exit code. No test plan section, no chat narrative, no security commentary, no release-type opinion. The PR stays a draft: nobody said ready is the signal, and no gate ran on a detached checkout.
expectations: Agent pushes and opens the PR without asking again, because the request named both in one sentence

Agent checks after the commit that the committed tree is the staged tree and that nothing is left unstaged before putting the commit's sha on the verify run; if either check fails it labels the run 'working tree before commit' and gates the commit detached before the push
Agent runs pr-desc in create mode and hands it the verify report block and the pushed head sha
PR is opened as a draft
PR title is a Conventional Commit subject, for example feat(auth): add token refresh
PR body contains a Summary section, a Trade-offs section and a Follow-ups section
PR body contains a Verification section whose bullets each name a command that ran, the head it ran on and its exit code
PR body contains NO '## Test Plan' section and no how-to-test checklist
PR body contains no chat narrative, security-review commentary, or release-type or version-bump opinion
PR body contains no Claude session link, model name or other AI identifier
Agent does NOT mark the PR ready, since the request did not say ready is the review signal
Agent reports the PR URL and that it is a draft

evals.prompt: Commit all unstaged changes in /tmp/eval-ship-5-ws. Ignore "notes.local.md".
evals.expected_output: Agent branches first if on main, then stages everything except notes.local.md, and also excludes .claude/, docs/plans/ and .plans/. It shows the staged file list so the exclusions are visible, then commits with a conventional message. notes.local.md remains modified but unstaged afterwards. No push and no PR.
expectations: Agent excludes notes.local.md from staging as the user requested
Agent also excludes .claude/, docs/plans/ and .plans/ without being asked
Agent shows the staged file list before committing so exclusions are visible
The commit does not contain notes.local.md
Agent uses a conventional commit message
Agent does NOT push and does NOT open a pull request

evals.prompt: Push, draft PR, gate on a clean checkout, mark ready. The repo is /tmp/eval-ship-6-ws, the commit is already on feat/ledger-add-export and make validate is the gate.
evals.expected_output: Agent treats the one sentence as the go-ahead for every step it names and asks no question between them. Finding nothing to stage and the commit already ahead of origin/main, it skips the commit step rather than stopping at 'nothing to commit', and continues with the head that exists. It pushes the branch, runs pr-desc in create mode with the verify report block and the head sha, and opens a draft PR. It then fetches origin/feat/ledger-add-export, checks that head out detached into a throwaway worktree from mktemp, runs make validate there with the output and exit code captured under the task worktree's .verify-logs/, and removes the throwaway worktree. With exit 0 it hands the run to pr-desc in refresh mode so Verification gains the detached bullet, then runs gh pr ready. The report names the head sha, the gate command, its exit code and the tail of its output.
expectations: Agent asks no confirmation question between the push, the PR, the gate and the ready flip
Agent finds nothing to stage, sees the commit already ahead of origin/main, skips the commit step and does NOT stop with 'nothing to commit'
Agent pushes before opening the PR and opens it as a draft
Agent creates a detached worktree at the pushed head sha, taken from origin/<branch> after a fetch, in a throwaway directory
Agent runs make validate inside the detached worktree, not in the task worktree, and captures its exit code
Agent removes the throwaway worktree after the gate, whatever the result
Agent runs gh pr ready only after the detached gate exited 0 on the pushed head
Agent hands the detached gate run to pr-desc so the PR body's Verification section records it with the head sha and exit code
Agent does NOT mark the PR ready on the strength of a run in the task worktree alone
Report states the head sha, the gate command, its exit code and the tail of its output

evals.prompt: main has moved since PR 31 went up in /tmp/eval-ship-7-ws and the PR now conflicts. Rebase feat/ledger-add-export and push.
evals.expected_output: Agent fetches origin, records the old head of origin/feat/ledger-add-export, and checks with git merge-base --is-ancestor that the fetched tip is contained in local HEAD before rewriting anything; had it not been, it would stop and show both sides instead of rebasing. It runs git rebase origin/main rather than merging main in, resolves the conflict by reading both sides, runs the verify git-state checks and the repo's gate on the rebased tree, then runs git range-diff between the old branch range and the rebased one and confirms no commit shows as dropped. It pushes with --force-with-lease=feat/ledger-add-export:<old-sha>, stating beforehand that origin/feat/ledger-add-export moves from the old sha to the new one and that the range-diff pairs every commit. It never runs a bare git push --force and never offers commit counts alone as the proof. It compares the three-dot diff with the PR body and runs pr-desc in update mode only if the conflict resolution changed the diff.
expectations: Agent fetches origin and records the old sha of origin/feat/ledger-add-export before rebasing
Agent checks that the fetched remote tip is an ancestor of local HEAD before the rebase, and would stop on divergence rather than rebase over it
Agent runs git rebase onto origin/main and does NOT run git merge main or git pull without --rebase
Agent resolves the conflict by reading both sides rather than taking one side wholesale or skipping the commit
Agent checks for a stalled rebase, unresolved paths and conflict markers before calling the rebase complete
Agent runs the repo's gate on the rebased tree before pushing
Agent runs git range-diff over the old and rebased ranges and confirms no commit is missing before pushing
Agent pushes with --force-with-lease=<branch>:<old-sha> and never with a bare --force
Agent states before the push that no commit is discarded, citing the range-diff rather than commit counts alone
Agent checks whether the three-dot diff changed and runs pr-desc in update mode only if it did

evals.prompt: PR 31 merged in /tmp/eval-ship-8-ws, clean up. The worktree is .claude/worktrees/feat+ledger-add-export.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs gh pr view 31 and confirms state is MERGED, taking headRefOid as the merged head. Before deleting anything it compares the local branch tip, the remote branch tip and the worktree's status against that head; a tip beyond it or uncommitted work is a stop with the extra commits listed. With all three clean it removes the worktree from the main checkout, deletes the local branch with -D because squash-merge means -d would refuse, deletes the remote branch with a lease on the merged head, and prunes. It writes a short hand-over note with the PR number, merge commit, what landed and what is left. The report pastes the Deleted branch line, the [deleted] line and the worktree list afterwards rather than offering an empty git branch --list as proof.
expectations: Agent runs gh pr view on PR 31 and checks that state is MERGED before any deletion
Agent reads the merged head sha from the PR and compares the local branch tip against it before deleting the branch
Agent compares the remote branch tip against the merged head and checks the worktree for uncommitted work before removing it
Agent would stop and list the commits beyond the merged head rather than delete a branch that advanced after the merge
Agent removes the worktree from the main checkout with git -C rather than from inside the worktree, without --force
Agent deletes the local branch only after the MERGED and tip checks and pastes the 'Deleted branch' line
Agent deletes the remote branch with --force-with-lease on the merged head, and only if ls-remote still lists it
Agent writes a hand-over note naming the PR number, the merge commit, what landed and what is left
Agent pastes git worktree list after the removal as evidence
Agent does NOT offer an empty git branch --list on its own as proof that the branch was deleted
